interstellar-ships.own_why: You get a place no government could reach once under way, but not within 25 years, because no crewed ship exists or has funding. The registering state's control also has no end point in the Outer Space Treaty, so the crew's law would hold only by distance.

the-sun.own_why: You get a notary's record and online plot sales, but no place, because no one can go to the Sun or live there.

outer-moons.own_why: You get a place months or years from any navy, but no realistic way to get there in 25 years, because every plan is a paper study. Licensing and registry law would also still follow the settlers from Earth.

venus-clouds.own_why: You get a study of floating habitats about 55 km up, but no settlement, because nothing has flown and NASA's HAVOC study went unfunded. Any craft would also sit on a state's register.

mars-and-beyond.own_why: You get distance that would slow outside control by months, but not your own law by right, because the registering state keeps legal power under Article VIII and licenses the ships that keep the settlement alive. The transport and food systems also do not exist yet.

asteroids.own_why: You get ownership of mined material under a few national laws, but no right to the asteroid and no settlement, because no one has lived on one and the two mining companies set up to reach them ran short of money. Any crew would stay under a registering state.

moon.own_why: You get a possible base with a safety zone around it, but no title and no separate law, because Article II bars any claim and the licensing state keeps control of the base and crew. Three days from Earth is close enough for supply lines to be cut.

lagrange-cislunar.own_why: You get a possible station in a stable spot, but not your own law, because the same registry and licensing rules apply as in low orbit and the station depends on supplies from Earth. No private habitat has been built there.

geo.own_why: You get a slot and frequencies only through a member state's filing, and not your own law, because that state answers for the station and can drop it. No habitat at this height has been funded.

orbital-megastructures.own_why: You get designs dating from 1975, but no structure and no separate law, because none has been funded and a large station would stay on a state's register. An elevator's anchor would also sit within some state's reach.

leo.own_why: You get a real chance of living in a private station, but not your own law, because the registering state keeps legal power over the object and everyone on it. Rules among residents would only be contracts under that state's law.

stratosphere-near-space.own_why: You get a possible craft at about 20 km, but no one can live on it long, and no legal shelter, because over land it counts as that country's airspace and it needs a register and a launch site. The US shot down a Chinese balloon at this height in 2023.

airborne-habitats.own_why: You get uncrewed test craft, but no home, because no one lives permanently in the air. Any aircraft answers to the state that registers it and has to come down somewhere.

airspace-over-high-seas.own_why: You get freedom to fly, but no place of your own, because the aircraft's state of registry has power over crimes on board. Fuel and maintenance also force landings in some country.

airspace-over-states.own_why: You get a flight permit at most, because Article 1 of the Chicago Convention gives the country below complete sovereignty over its air. That country can order the craft down.

ships-flag.own_why: You get a real home at sea with shared rules, but not your own law, because the flag state's law applies on board and it can strike the ship off its register. This fails the third test by design, as MS The World accepts.

high-seas.own_why: You get water no country owns and few states nearby, but no right to it and no protection, because Article 89 bars any claim and Article 110 lets a warship board a ship with no flag. Your law would apply only while no government chooses to act, and a real flag would replace it with that state's law.

central-arctic-ocean-and-svalbard.own_why: You get the right to live on Svalbard or a hard camp on moving sea ice, but not your own law, because Norway is sovereign on Svalbard and the ice cannot support a lasting settlement without heavy state support. A US court tried a killing on the T-3 ice island.

floating-ice.own_why: You get unsettled law on who holds an iceberg, but no lasting ground, because ice moves and melts and stations on it have run only with state support for months or a few years. A23a, once the largest iceberg, was gone or nearly gone by July 2026.

new-land.own_why: You get ground for a short time at best, but rarely ground no state holds, because new land nearly always rises on some country's seabed and most of it washes away. Graham Island lasted about six months and two countries claimed it within weeks.

eez-shelf.own_why: You get free passage, but no right to stay on a structure, because Article 60 gives the coastal state exclusive power over artificial islands in its zone. The Thai navy raided the XLII home off Phuket in 2019, and its occupants faced charges carrying life in prison or death.

territorial-sea.own_why: You get a building project under the coastal state's law, and nothing else, because that state has full sovereignty in the belt. With a special law it becomes a host's zone and carries a host's limits.

reefs-low-tide-elevations.own_why: You get a cheap physical base, but no title and little time, because a feature under water at high tide cannot be claimed and nearby states have acted within months. Tonga annexed Minerva in 1972 and the shelf rules stopped other projects.

abandoned-platforms.own_why: You get a deck you can physically hold, but not law that others accept, because the coastal state holds power over installations on its shelf and Italy destroyed Rose Island within months. Sealand's history came from a three-mile limit that no longer exists, and it has only one or two residents.

disputed-islands.own_why: You get nothing a garrison will let you keep, because several states already hold these islands with armed forces. Each claimant treats a newcomer as an intruder on its own land, as Tomás Cloma's arrest in 1974 showed.

undersea-water-column.own_why: You get a licensed habitat, but not your own law, because a fixed habitat needs the coastal state's permission and a moving one needs a flag. Going deep gives concealment, not legal shelter, and no one has lived long below the surface beyond national waters.

deep-seabed-area.own_why: You get a mining contract under a sponsoring state at most, and no territory, because Article 137 bars any claim and the International Seabed Authority licenses only state-backed operators. No people live there.

underground-subseabed.own_why: You get a private bunker under local law, but not your own law, because land ownership and a coastal state's shelf rights both run downward. German police raided CyberBunker in 2019 and its operators were prosecuted.

inland-waters.own_why: You get an island only with the permission of the state holding it, because every lake and river lies inside or between countries. A treaty you did not sign can reassign an island, as Lausanne did with Ada Kaleh, and a dam can drown it.

terra-nullius-land.own_why: You get land no state currently asserts, but not the right to it or a way in, because only states can acquire such land and each site is reached only through states that enforce their own law. Liberland's camp was cleared in 2023 under Croatian police watch, and Bir Tawil has no water. A state could still occupy such land under the old rule, which is the second figure.

antarctica-unclaimed.own_why: You get the one large piece of land no country claims, but no right to it, because Article IV of the Antarctic Treaty bars new claims and access runs through treaty members. No claimant has built anything there.

antarctica-claimed.own_why: You get a possible campaign base, but not your own law, because seven states hold frozen claims and treaty members must give notice of expeditions from their soil. Greenpeace ran the only non-government year-round base and removed it in the early 1990s.

inside-state.own_why: You get a flag, titles and often decades of being left alone, but not your own law, because the country's tax and criminal law keep applying. Hutt River's owners were ordered to pay millions in tax after 50 years, and toleration is not control.

host-state-carve-outs.own_why: You get separate commercial law, courts and tax if a government agrees, but rarely criminal law or lasting control, because Dubai's financial centre leaves criminal law with the host and Honduras's top court voided the ZEDE laws in 2024. This is still the highest figure, since a host can in principle hand over all of it and no one else can.

unrecognised-state.own_why: You get real law and courts if you hold the ground, since recognition is not needed, but a private group has no way to get there, because every current case came from war, collapse or foreign protection. A people with a movement, an army or a patron does far better, though Artsakh ended within days.

buffer-zones.own_why: You get a home among earlier residents at most, and no law of your own, because peacekeepers or armies control entry and the surrounding states keep their claims. No declared state in such a zone has been found.

buy-from-a-state.own_why: You get ordinary ownership with the host's law still on it, and sovereignty only if a government signs it over by treaty, because a land sale does not move the right to rule. No private purchase has done this since the old grants, and Minerva, Atlantis and Bakov all found no seller. States do buy from states, most recently in 1963.

leases-and-extraterritorial-spots.own_why: You get a tenant's position under the host's law, but not authority, because the leases that carry their own law run between states. Guantánamo has lasted since 1903 on that basis, and the second figure is for a state using it.

run-by-international-agreement.own_why: You get nothing as a private group, because only a treaty or the UN Security Council can create such a place. States can create one, as with Danzig or Tangier, and each lasted only while the powers behind it agreed.

secession-and-decolonisation.own_why: You get no route as a private group, because secession needs a population already on the land and consent cannot be bought. A people with a real movement can gain full own law and courts, and this is the route that has produced new states, usually only with the parent state's agreement or loss of power.

taking-over-a-state-or-town.own_why: You get local offices by moving voters, which fails because the state's law sits above a town, or a whole country's law by force, which would meet every test but nearly always ends in arrests. Denard's 11 years in the Comoros needed outside backing and a recognised president, and it still ended.

indigenous-prior-sovereignty.own_why: You get nothing as a newcomer, because the claim belongs to a people and cannot be acquired. A people can win land, courts and self-rule, as with Nunavut and McGirt, but the existing state's law stays above them, so few would pass the third test.

exile-and-landless-authority.own_why: You get elections, a community and an office abroad, but no place, because someone else holds the land and the host's law applies to the office. An exile body with a real people has very rarely returned to govern, as Tibet's has not.

digital-no-territory.own_why: You get members, tokens and a company shell, but no place and no law over anyone, because every member and server stays under the law of where it sits. Network School lost its Malaysian licence in July 2026.

no-territory-conceptual.own_why: You get a name and an organisation that can last, but no place, because nothing is held on the ground. Members remain under the ordinary law of wherever they live.

combo-no-flag-vessel.own_why: You get a boat no state has listed and your own rules aboard, but no protection, because Article 110 lets any warship board it and courts have treated such vessels as having no rights. Ports and insurers also refuse them, so ten years is unlikely.

combo-tethered-platform-high-seas.own_why: You get a structure no treaty clearly classifies, but only an argument and not a right, because Article 89 bars any claim and supply boats call at ports where they can be pressured. It costs at least about $50 million and has to survive waves, which broke the Aisland barge.

combo-unrecognised-flag.own_why: You get a painted flag, but no nationality for the ship, because courts look for a state behind it and treat the rest as stateless. Taiwan's flag works only because a real government stands behind it.

combo-company-run-flag.own_why: You get ordinary registration through a company, but no special terms, because nationality comes from the state and a registry firm cannot grant it. The flag state's law still applies on board.

combo-always-moving-habitat.own_why: You get a lasting home at sea, but not your own law, because a flagged ship is under its flag state and any port's law on arrival. MS The World shows it can last, and it does so as a Bahamian ship.

combo-seabed-structure-no-mining.own_why: You get a possible gap in seabed licensing, but no ground and little chance of building, because Article 137 bars owning any part of the floor and the deepest habitat on record went to 610 feet.

combo-shallow-bank-unresolved-shelf.own_why: You get cheaper anchoring on free water, but no secure seabed, because the floor is usually claimed as extended shelf and Article 60 then applies. Two groups aimed at Saya de Malha and got no more than a steel frame, and it would depend on two governments doing nothing.

combo-new-island-beyond-eez.own_why: You get land that might belong to no one if one ever rises and lasts, but not a right to it, because only a state can acquire it by occupation. Almost no land appears beyond every coastal zone.

combo-low-tide-with-claimant.own_why: You get a building permit from one claimant, but not your own law, because you stand under that claimant's law and the others dispute it. Malaysia revoked the Layang-Layang resort's licence in 2025.

combo-buy-grandfathered-structure.own_why: You get possession of an old fort, but not a transferable state, because a sale passes possession only and Sealand has been inside British waters since 1987. Britain has tolerated a family with one or two residents, and a real community would draw a different response.

combo-eez-permit-own-charter.own_why: You get a lawful platform with whatever special rules the coastal state grants, but rarely criminal law or a promise that lasts, because Article 60 keeps exclusive jurisdiction with that state and a later law can undo the charter. No state has agreed to this at sea, and French Polynesia withdrew in 2018.

combo-drifting-ice-no-flag.own_why: You get unsettled law on the ice, but no protection and no lasting ground, because it melts and drifts and people have lived on it only with heavy state support or for a season.

combo-antarctica-outside-treaty.own_why: You get a thin argument that Article IV does not bind outsiders, but no ground to stand on, because that argument gives a private person no title and access runs through treaty countries. Only governments and Greenpeace have kept year-round bases.

combo-antarctic-floating-ice.own_why: You get an open question about whether a berg counts as high seas, but no lasting ground, because bergs crack and melt and only state programs have kept people on Antarctic ice.

combo-submersible-beyond-waters.own_why: You get concealment for a while, but no status, because a flagged submersible is under its flag state and an unflagged one meant to avoid detection comes close to a crime under American law. No private group has lived long this way.

combo-government-service-ship.own_why: You get Article 96's strong protection, but it belongs to the state that owns and runs the ship, because residents who pay for one do not make it theirs. That state's law applies on board, and no one is known to have arranged this.

combo-high-seas-pocket.own_why: You get high seas water, but no shelter from the states around it, because one neighbour controls nearly every approach and the seabed may be theirs, as Russia's is under the Peanut Hole. A ship there still answers to its flag.

combo-platform-with-sinking-state.own_why: You get a platform under a real state's law, but not your own, because the sovereignty stays with that state and Article 60(8) gives the platform no island status. Kiribati's 2011 idea had a $2 billion cost and no funder, and the state itself could build one, which is the second figure.

combo-unflagged-sea-launch.own_why: You get a launch attempt at most, and no place to live, because the platform can be boarded and the rocket on no register has no state to defend it. Parts, ports and radio links each pass through a government first.

combo-flag-of-convenience-launch-ship.own_why: You get a working launch business, as Sea Launch ran 36 times, but no territory, because a real flag state and a real licensing state stand over it. It is a service, not a place to live.

combo-air-launch-open-ocean.own_why: You get a launch method, as Pegasus shows, but no place, because the aircraft has to land often and stays on a state's register.

combo-unrecognised-state-in-space.own_why: You get nothing new on the ground, because this needs an unrecognised government first and the UN system has no place for its launches. No such place has reached orbit.

combo-digital-nation-satellite.own_why: You get a small satellite and a membership list, but no place where people live, because Asgardia's satellite stays under its launching and registering state. Members remain under the law where they stand.

combo-buy-orbiting-station.own_why: You get ownership of hardware if a seller agrees, but not your own law, because the state of registry keeps control after a sale. No crewed station has been sold to a private owner, and MirCorp only leased rights.

combo-mars-contract.own_why: You get a clause between customer and company, but no law that binds a government, because a contract cannot release treaty duties. The community stays under the licensing state, and nobody has gone to Mars.

combo-resources-stepping-stone.own_why: You get ownership of what you extract under four countries' laws, but no right to the ground, because none of those laws grants one. No one has mined anything in space and mining firms have run out of money.

combo-sea-anchored-elevator.own_why: You get a design with no material strong enough to build it, and major powers would act at once on anything so valuable. It would also rest on an anchor with no agreed legal category.

combo-launch-from-non-party-state.own_why: You get a launch site in a friendly host, but not your own law, because the site stays under that host and founders stay under their home laws. OTRAG's tests in Africa ended without reaching orbit.

combo-launch-from-unclaimed-land.own_why: You get a claim to launch from Bir Tawil or Marie Byrd Land, but no way to supply it, because access runs through neighbours or treaty logistics. A rocket from there would draw immediate attention.

combo-leased-spaceport.own_why: You get a launch site on rented land, but as a private lessee only under the host's law, because the deals that carry their own law, such as Baikonur, are between states. The second figure is for a state doing this.

combo-unregistered-orbit.own_why: You get an object on no list, but no legal gain, because the launching state stays responsible whether it registers or not. A crewed one is far harder and has no protection.

combo-small-state-station.own_why: You get a real register and a friendly small state, which could in principle hand over its law by statute, but not independence from it, because that state answers for the station under Article VI. The launch provider's own government can also refuse.

combo-igo-register.own_why: You get a valid form of registration, as ESA uses, but not your own law, because the member states would keep control and carry the liability. Getting several governments to accept unlimited liability for a private project is the hard part.

combo-lease-on-station.own_why: You get the form most likely to be built, a contract among residents, but it fails the third test, because the state of registry's law stands above any lease.

combo-salvage-derelict.own_why: You get old hardware if the owner agrees, but no title without consent, because Article VIII keeps ownership in place. Only consented recovery has happened.

combo-born-in-space.own_why: You get a nationality question and no territory, because nationality laws handle such children through their parents. A birth in space would add a resident and give the settlement no law of its own.

combo-in-situ-habitat.own_why: You get a genuine gap in the treaties for an object never launched, but not your own law, because Article VI still covers the people and their activities. The technology is far from ready.

combo-captured-asteroid-home.own_why: You get a possible claim to extracted material, but not to the rock, and no way to do it soon, because no one has moved an asteroid and NASA cancelled its one mission. Governments would stop the licence long before arrival.

combo-below-100-km.own_why: You get no place, because air at this height is too thin to float in and too thick to orbit through. National licensing laws reach citizens at any height.

combo-unregistered-airship.own_why: You get a craft that does not exist, and no right to enter any country's air, because an aircraft with no register has none. Any resupply or emergency meets a state at once.

combo-unrecognised-state-aircraft.own_why: You get flights at most and no place, because treaty rights depend on being a contracting state. KTHY lost in the English courts even with Turkish backing.

combo-haps-over-high-seas.own_why: You get an uncrewed platform flying under national permission, but no home, because no crewed version exists and the craft stays on a register. Loon closed for lack of a business.

combo-settlement-by-outsiders.own_why: You get a founder from a country outside the treaties, but not freedom from them in practice, because nearly all rockets and launch sites belong to treaty members and custom may bind anyway. Reaching the Moon stays the main barrier.

combo-host-state-leaves-treaty.own_why: You get a real state claiming space land for itself, but the law would be that state's and not yours, because a private group is only its guest. No party has left the treaty, and other states' launchers stay bound.

combo-safety-zone-possession.own_why: You get practical control of a Moon site if a state backs you, but not your own law, because safety zones rest on non-binding principles and that state's licence. Article II rules out any title.

combo-colony-declares-independence.own_why: You get a declaration that is not unlawful in itself and hard to reverse at a distance, but no settlement to make it, because self-sufficient colonies within 25 years are very unlikely. Article VIII also keeps the registering state in control on paper.

combo-company-special-district.own_why: You get real local power over land, roads and utilities, but not your own law, because state and national law apply throughout. Reedy Creek lasted 56 years and then its board was taken over by the state.

combo-tribal-partnership.own_why: You get a guest's place under a tribe's immunity, but not your own law, because the immunity belongs to the tribe and Congress can end it. It gives an outside founder nothing personal, as courts have held.

combo-investment-treaty-shield.own_why: You get a money claim years later, but not the zone back, because a tribunal can award damages and cannot restore power to make law. Próspera's claim is still pending and Honduras's court has already voided the underlying law.

combo-associated-state-deal.own_why: You get nothing as a private group without first being given a territory, because every association grew out of a colonial or trust territory. A real territory can get full lawmaking, as the Cook Islands have since 1965, usually after a long process and a constitutional change by the partner.

combo-small-state-lease.own_why: You get land and possibly your own rules by statute from a needy government, but the grant lasts only as long as its politics, because a small state can give what it holds and then take it back. Vanuatu said Satoshi Island's tokens gave no rights, while Laos's 99-year Golden Triangle lease is the closest case, under Lao law and US sanctions.

combo-treaty-cession-new-body.own_why: You get the only clean title that meets every test, but almost no chance of it, because no state has ceded land to a new private body in modern times. Treaty transfers even between states have stalled, as with Tiran and Chagos, and a body that is not yet a state may have no capacity to receive one.

combo-buy-then-cession.own_why: You get ordinary ownership first, but ownership does not lead to a right to rule, because no modern government has handed that to a private owner. Liechtenstein and Sarawak worked when rulers could give such rights.

combo-headquarters-immunity.own_why: You get immune premises for a valued job, but not courts or citizenship, because these agreements protect functions and host law still governs daily life. Hosts have not given them to a body that only wants to govern itself.

combo-data-embassy.own_why: You get a protected server room if a state hosts it for a state, but no people and no law, because it exists to keep records safe. No non-state version has been done.

combo-religious-status.own_why: You get land and a town under general law, and sometimes long patience, but not your own law, because Kiryas Joel and Colorado City show courts stepping in. Vatican City and Mount Athos rest on a history no new group has.

combo-sez-private-charter.own_why: You get a privately run zone with commercial courts, but rarely criminal law, because the designs that last ask for less and the one that claimed general government was voided in Honduras in 2024. Freeport has lasted since 1955 and a tribunal in 2026 still rejected its claim of exclusive authority.

combo-popup-rotation.own_why: You get a yearly gathering with a shared culture, but no place, because the group moves and each host's law applies during each stay.

combo-voters-and-charter.own_why: You get a town council and a city charter, but only what state law allows, because legislatures can change those powers. Starbase is an ordinary Texas city, and criminal acts ended Rajneeshpuram.

combo-bankrupt-village.own_why: You get private land under normal law, and no governing power, because state law controls municipal status. Buford, Wyoming was sold as property.

combo-two-state-condominium.own_why: You get nothing as a private group beyond running a mine or dam under the authority, because only two states can create one and they keep the sovereignty. Two states can do it, as the second figure reflects, and Neutral Moresnet ended at the Treaty of Versailles.

combo-old-title-revival.own_why: You get a family title on paper, but no land and no law, because the Palmas rule favours whoever governs now and the Hague and Paris decisions gave claimants nothing. Peoples with real treaties have slightly more to work with.

combo-floating-host-zone.own_why: You get a floating zone with a host's consent, but it stays the host's territory and law, because any special rules exist by that host's statute and a floating zone is easy to close. French Polynesia ended its deal in 2018, and Busan claims no independence.

combo-treaty-colony.own_why: You get nothing as a private group, because only states make such treaties, and the models keep sovereignty with one state. Åland shows strong self-rule for an existing people, though Finland keeps sovereignty and most criminal law, and Svalbard gives no right to rule.

combo-treaty-buffer-land.own_why: You get nothing as a private group, because treaty buffers belong to the states that made them and you would be removed without both sides' consent. Even those states can end them on notice, as Jordan did at Baqura.

combo-leased-private-operator.own_why: You get operating control of valuable land, but police and courts stay with the host, because a commercial lease does not move authority. Panama's court ended a concession in 2026 and Australia is seeking to buy Darwin back.

combo-private-force.own_why: You get short control of ground at most, because laws in the US, Britain, South Africa and France reach funders and recruits and nearly every attempt has ended in arrests. Holding land against a state by force is a crime for everyone involved, and it could only meet the tests by beating the state.

combo-flag-theory.own_why: You get a spread of passports, bank accounts and residences, but no place, because each country's law still applies to the part of your life in it.

combo-renounce-stateless.own_why: You get no nationality, and no place, because a stateless person has no right to enter anywhere and stays under the law of wherever they are.

combo-cbi-private-community.own_why: You get a bought passport and a private estate, but not your own law, because both sit under the host's law. No group has combined a shared nationality with a governing charter.

combo-e-residency-entity.own_why: You get a lawful Estonian company and online services, but no place, because the company sits under Estonian law and members live under their own.

combo-dao-shell.own_why: You get a legal entity cheaply, but no place and no government powers, because these statutes grant none and courts have looked through unregistered DAOs. A plot of land held by one stays under local law.

combo-arbitration-private-law.own_why: You get private courts whose civil awards have real force, but no place and no criminal law, because the New York Convention covers people who signed and state courts keep the final word. Próspera used this inside a host's zone.

combo-private-currency-treasury.own_why: You get a token or coin, but no place, because money does not give territory. Liberty Dollar and Liberty Reserve show prosecution when private money reaches the public at scale.

combo-observer-status.own_why: You get a standing at international meetings if you have centuries of history or a treaty role, but no place, because that status comes with no land. A new group winning it is very unlikely.

combo-treaty-organisation.own_why: You get a treaty body with an office if friendly states ratify one, but not your own law, because the member states and the host keep control. The Global Green Growth Institute did this with a president's backing, and it runs an organisation, not a place.

combo-network-plots.own_why: You get real land and towns with a shared culture, but each plot stays under local law, because private title does not move the right to rule. The Jewish National Fund's purchases did not themselves produce a state.

combo-unrecognised-treaties.own_why: You get a signed paper among unrecognised bodies, but no place and no new power, because no outside government is bound by it.

combo-exile-new-community.own_why: You get a charter and elections abroad, but no land, because exile standing rests on a real state or people and a new community has neither. The host's law applies.

combo-charter-ship.own_why: You get a ship where everyone has signed one contract, but it fails the third test, because the flag state's law stands above any contract. Residents stay residents of their home countries to banks and tax offices.

combo-partial-passport.own_why: You get a travel paper a few states might honour, but no place, because a passport comes from a state or from states' agreement. Nansen worked for refugees, and no new private group has won that.

combo-digital-continuity.own_why: You get a digital archive, but no place and no continuity promise, because the promises in ICJ paragraph 363 and resolution 80/263 speak of an established state such as Tuvalu. A new private group has neither.

combo-landless-state-host.own_why: You get a contract with a state that has lost land, but its status is the state's and not yours, and any land it holds lies under a host's law, as Kiribati's plot in Fiji does. The second figure is for that state rebuilding a place of its own.

combo-finance-no-recognition.own_why: You get a banking channel at best, and no place, because this is a service for a place that already exists. Somaliland relies on remittance firms and a new project with no economy starts far behind them.

combo-rented-sovereign.own_why: You get a real state's power over one function, such as a ship register, but not a place or a law of your own, because the state keeps the power and can end the contract. Stretching it to courts and criminal law turns it into a host's zone, with a host's limits.
